_about: Bat-bomb film continuity database. Every shot prompt must copy the design-lock text of each character/location it uses, and record the state it leaves behind (positions, props, damage, time of day). The storyboard (Stage 4) adds one entry per shot under 'shots'.

film.style_lock: 2D hand-drawn animated feature film, cel-shaded characters with clean ink outlines and soft painted shading, richly detailed painterly backgrounds, cinematic lighting, warm 1940s American period detail, slightly exaggerated expressive proportions. No text anywhere.

hero_bat.lock: small Mexican free-tailed bat, warm grey-brown fur, lighter tan chest, dark charcoal leathery wings with visible finger bones, two big rounded ears with pink-brown insides, short wrinkled snout with a dark nose, large glossy dark-brown eyes with white highlight, slightly worried eyebrows, thin free tail. No clothes. Never talks.
hero_bat.scale: fits in a human palm; wingspan about one hand-length
hero_bat.props: from the Muroc test on: tiny grey cylindrical capsule clipped to its chest

adams.lock: Dr. Lytle 'Doc' Adams, 61, short and round-bellied, balding with a grey fringe, round wire-rimmed glasses, rosy cheeks, big friendly grin, brown three-piece wool suit, white shirt, small red bow tie, brown fedora with dark band, brown shoes.

fieser.lock: Dr. Louis Fieser, 44, tall and lean, neat dark-brown hair combed back with a side part, clean-shaven narrow face, thin dark eyebrows, serious focused look, white knee-length lab coat over grey waistcoat and dark tie, grey trousers, black shoes.

rancher.lock: old New Mexico rancher, tall and wiry, tanned wrinkled face, white stubble, bushy white moustache, pale-blue squinting eyes, battered tan cowboy hat, faded blue work shirt with rolled sleeves, brown suspenders, worn blue denim jeans, dusty brown boots.

epler.lock: TO DESIGN in Stage 3: Lt. Col. R. Bruce Epler, Army Chemical Warfare Service officer, khaki uniform

couffer.lock: TO DESIGN in Stage 3: Jack Couffer, teenage junior bat scientist

base_commander.lock: TO DESIGN in Stage 3: full colonel, Carlsbad auxiliary field

fdr.lock: TO DESIGN in Stage 3: stylised, respectful; only shown reading/writing the documented note

carlsbad_cave_dusk.lock: huge dark cave mouth in a rocky New Mexico hillside, scrub, yucca and boulders, orange-violet sunset

carlsbad_aux_field.lock: brand-new 1943 wooden auxiliary airfield: tall wooden control tower with glass cab on a lattice frame, long wooden barracks, curved-roof hangars, sandy airstrip, distant mesas, hard blue sky

muroc_lakebed.lock: vast flat white cracked dry lakebed, distant blue mountains, hard morning light, long shadows

ranch_porch.lock: shaded weathered wooden front porch of a 1940s New Mexico ranch house, porch posts, dark ceiling boards, bright desert yard and red barn behind

props.h2_capsule: tiny grey cylindrical napalm capsule (about forefinger-joint size) clipped to a bat's chest skin
props.ice_tray: shallow metal tray of crushed ice holding sleeping bats
props.bomb_shell: five-foot steel cylinder with stacked round trays of bats inside, parachute pack on top
props.b25: North American B-25 bomber, olive drab
